issues.legal_issue: A termination notice sent by registered post to a corporate tenant is presumed served when a disputed acknowledgment cannot be linked to that notice and the company does not rebut service.
material_facts: The landlords sent registered-post notices to three defendants, including the company that was the tenant, and produced three postal receipts.
Only one acknowledgment receipt was produced, and an individual defendant denied the signature on it; the acknowledgment was not shown to relate to the notice sent to the company.
The address was admitted to be correct, and the company did not state that it had not received a notice.
issues.conclusion: Service of the termination notice on the company was presumed, and the notice sent by registered post to the company satisfied the applicable notice requirement.
issues.legal_principle: Section 106, paragraph two, of the Transfer of Property Act permits a written notice to be sent by post to the party intended to be bound; the notice requirement in Section 12(2) of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act is to be met in that manner. Service may be presumed under Section 27 of the General Clauses Act and Section 114 of the Evidence Act. Under Green View Radio Service v. Laxmibai Ramji, a credible denial by an addressee that an acknowledgment bears their signature may rebut the presumption and shift the burden to the sender; here, the denial related only to one unlinked acknowledgment, not to the notice sent to the company.

rule.if: tenancy_termination_possession_case and registered_notice_sent_to_tenant and disputed_acknowledgment_not_linked_to_tenant_notice and tenant_does_not_rebut_receipt

predicates.tenancy_termination_possession_case: The proceeding seeks possession of rented premises on the basis of termination of the tenancy.
predicates.registered_notice_sent_to_tenant: The landlord sent the termination notice to the tenant by registered post.
predicates.disputed_acknowledgment_not_linked_to_te: A disputed acknowledgment does not establish that it relates to the notice sent to the tenant whose service is at issue.
predicates.tenant_does_not_rebut_receipt: The tenant does not otherwise deny or rebut receipt of the notice.

issues.definition: When a possession proceeding depends on termination of a tenancy, a registered notice sent to the tenant is presumed served if a disputed acknowledgment is not linked to that notice and the tenant does not otherwise rebut receipt.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant seeking to avoid a possession decree for rent default must meet the applicable rent-payment requirements through the suit and appeal.
material_facts: The landlords sought possession in a rent-control proceeding on the ground of rent default.
The tenant had not deposited the full arrears by the first date of hearing.
The tenant did not pay rent month by month during the appeal.
The findings about those defaults were not successfully challenged.
issues.conclusion: The courts below were right to decree possession for rent default, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 12(3)(b) of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act imposes mandatory requirements that a tenant must strictly comply with during the suit and any appeal when possession is sought on that ground. The Court relied on no earlier case for this issue.

predicates.rent_control_possession_proceeding: The proceeding seeks possession of rented premises under a rent-control regime on the ground of rent default.
predicates.full_arrears_not_deposited_by_first_hear: The tenant did not pay or deposit all rent arrears by the first date of hearing.
predicates.rent_not_paid_during_appeal: The tenant did not continue paying rent during the appeal.

issues.definition: In a rent-control possession proceeding for rent default, failure to deposit all arrears by the first hearing and failure to pay rent during the appeal results in the possession decree being upheld for rent default.
